summary: Enterprise Suite AC-21 adds a review-only audit-chain emission contract for later Oyatie cloud integration. The plan defines CloudEvents-style required context attributes, W3C traceparent correlation, OpenTelemetry log-mapping intent, tenant/idempotency/payload-digest/evidence-ref extensions, nine tenant-scoped Enterprise Suite event schemas, digest-only payload rules, WAL/outbox/Merkle prerequisites, and cloud-readiness-gate composition while keeping WAL runtime, broker publish, Merkle sealing runtime, cloud audit sink, and runtime audit-chain emission as non-claims/blockers. The slice also normalizes the prior Postgres/RLS catalog row and ChainCoordinate data_class annotations so broad catalog/data-class gates can produce honest evidence.

findings: The slice is a deterministic contract crate plus readiness composition; no network, file, broker, WAL, sealer, or cloud sink side effects are introduced.
Validation rejects duplicate event types, missing CloudEvents/trace context metadata, credential-shaped context strings, and runtime-overclaim flags.
Audit emission is modeled as tenant-scoped, idempotent, digest-only event contracts with trace correlation and evidence refs before runtime transport is claimed.
The slice also normalizes catalog and data_class blockers so broad CI evidence can be made more honest.
Positive coverage asserts CloudEvents-style context, W3C traceparent, OpenTelemetry mapping intent, tenant/idempotency/payload digest extensions, and nonclaims.
Negative tests cover missing required metadata, duplicate event types, runtime audit-chain overclaims, bad coordinates, and credential-shaped source leakage.
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if required context/extension attributes, duplicate-event rejection, credential leak rejection, or runtime-overclaim guards are weakened.

findings: Developers can call enterprise_suite_audit_chain_emission_plan(), validate_enterprise_suite_audit_chain_emission_plan(), and render_audit_chain_emission_checklist() without credentials or runtime infrastructure.
Targeted audit-chain emission check/test/clippy PASS; cloud-readiness test/clippy PASS; 41-package enterprise regression test/clippy PASS; fmt, jq, quality-marker scan, and dependency-seam PASS.
Workspace catalog validation advanced past Enterprise Suite invalid-role rows but remains blocked by a pre-existing missing catalog row for oya-tenancy-tenant-lifecycle-kernel.
Workspace data_class gate advanced past audit-chain emission/sealing kernel annotation gaps but remains blocked by a pre-existing RebalanceTask.from_cell annotation gap.
Alternative rejected: attach a live WAL/broker/sealer runtime now; that would require external runtime proof and would overclaim the current local-only readiness stage.
Alternative rejected: generic untyped audit logs; they would not preserve tenant/idempotency/payload-digest/evidence-ref invariants needed for later cloud integration.
alternatives_named: store raw event payloads in audit context

findings: Credential-shaped context strings are rejected and audit payloads are digest-only, reducing leakage risk in event metadata that intermediaries may inspect.
Runtime flags remain false for WAL, broker publish, Merkle sealer, cloud sink, and runtime audit-chain emission.
The crate performs bounded Vec/BTreeSet validation over nine schemas only and adds no hot-path I/O, cryptography, or serialization runtime.

The contract preserves tenant partition, evidence reference, payload digest, and trace correlation metadata needed for later audit/compliance evidence without claiming statutory filing or runtime audit emission.
The slice is additive except for catalog/data_class normalization; removing the new crate and readiness fields restores prior behavior without migrations or runtime data changes.
The event schemas require traceparent, evidence refs, payload digests, event time, source, subject, and data schema metadata before later OpenTelemetry/cloud export.
No database or runtime migration is performed; WAL/outbox/Merkle/cloud sink work remains a future runtime slice.
Challenged assumption: adding an audit plan should clear runtime_audit_emission_missing. It intentionally does not; runtime proof still requires WAL/broker/sealer/cloud sink evidence.
The slice advances the Enterprise Suite path toward Oyatie cloud integration by defining audit event contracts and unblocking broad gate evidence while preserving honest nonclaims.
Package, crate, event types, catalog capability, and changeset use the existing Enterprise Suite naming pattern.
Spec AC-21, tasks plan/todo, multispectrum evidence, VCS transcript, and audit-chain rows document the new contract and nonclaims.
The crate is flat under microservices/enterprise-suite/crates and depends only on audit-chain emission API/kernel primitives.
The slice keeps a clean control-plane contract boundary and does not import storage, broker, network, or cloud adapters.
Only existing workspace path dependencies are used; no new third-party dependency is introduced.
Enterprise Suite spec JSON remains parseable and catalog rows use accepted role/plane/security-review vocabulary.
Validation is deterministic, bounded, and explicit about required metadata, uniqueness, credential leakage, and runtime-overclaim refusal.

W3C traceparent/tracestate propagation and trace correlation requirements.
